subject: general
question: If the sum of 10 observations is 12 and the sum of their squares is 18, then the standard deviation is:
solution:
The correct answer is 3/5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Standard deviation = sqrt{{{(x_i - bar x)}²} over n} = sqrt {Variance} 

Therefore, Variance V(X) = {1 over n} {{(x_i - bar x)}²} 

or, v(x)=(1)/(n)[Sigma(x_i²-2times x_i times bar x+bar x²)]

 =(Sigma x_i²)/(n)-2 bar x((Sigma x_i)/(n))+(Sigma bar x²)/(n)

= (Sigma x_i²)/(n)-2bar x²+(n.bar x²)/(n)

 = (Sigma x_i²)/(n)-2bar x²+bar x²

 V(x)=(Sigma x_i²)/(n)-bar x²

Given, the sum of 10 observations is 12 and the sum of their squares is 18. 

Thus, n = 10, sum x_i = 12, sum x_i² = 18 

Therefore, mean bar x = 1.2

Plugging this information into the equation of variance V(X), we have

 V(x)=(Sigma x_i²)/(n)-bar x²

=(1)/(10)times 18-(1.2)²

= 1.8 - 1.44

=0.36

Hence, the required standard deviation = sqrt {Variance} = sqrt{(0.36)} = 0.6 = {3 over 5}
